description: Pub. L. 41-271 substantive current-law chapter fragment

chapter_notes.heading: Codification
chapter_notes.text: Sections 5001 through 5007 consolidate title II of the Great Change Act of 2026, Pub. L. 41–271, including its amendments to the Streamlining and Protecting American Security Act and the National Security Act of 2026.

sections.heading: Individualized security-clearance eligibility
paragraphs: (a) No officer, employee, official, judge, Member of Congress, military officer, contractor, or other person shall receive or retain a security clearance solely by virtue of holding a public office, position of trust, military command, judicial assignment, congressional office, statutory office, employment title, or contract role.

(b) Any individual who requires access to classified information, Sensitive Compartmented Information, Special Access Program information, or any other protected national security information shall be subject to applicable clearance adjudication, vetting, need-to-know determination, and access approval procedures established by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence or another lawful security authority.

(c) Nothing in this paragraph shall be construed to prohibit the President, Vice President, Cabinet officials, congressional intelligence committee leadership, judges assigned to national security matters, military leaders, intelligence officials, or other senior officials from receiving access to classified information where such access is required for the performance of official duties, provided that such access is granted consistent with law, applicable security procedures, and need-to-know requirements.

(d) Access to classified information shall not be treated as automatic, permanent, inherited by office, or exempt from suspension, revocation, compartment restriction, or review by the Director of National Intelligence or the Director’s designee.

(e) The Director of National Intelligence may establish an expedited review process for individuals whose official duties require urgent or continuous access to classified information, provided that such expedited process shall not constitute an automatic clearance and shall remain subject to later review, suspension, limitation, or revocation.

(f) Nothing in this section shall be construed to deny necessary classified access to senior officials where such access is required for the lawful performance of official duties. This section shall only prohibit the automatic granting of a clearance, Sensitive Compartmented Information access, Special Access Program access, or other compartmented access without individualized adjudication, vetting, need-to-know review, or authorization by the appropriate security authority.

sections.heading: National security eligibility definitions and procedures
paragraphs: (a) Definitions.—For purposes of national security eligibility determinations:

(1) The term ‘security clearance’ means a formal determination that an individual is eligible to access classified information at a specified level, subject to need-to-know and any applicable compartmented access restrictions.

(2) The term ‘compartmented access’ means access to Sensitive Compartmented Information, Special Access Program information, or other controlled access information requiring additional authorization beyond a general clearance level.
(3) The term ‘need to know’ means a determination by an authorized holder of information that a prospective recipient requires access to specific information to perform lawful official duties.
(4) The term ‘eligibility determination’ shall not be construed to mean the automatic grant of a security clearance, compartmented access, or need-to-know authorization.

(b) National Security Council.—Nor shall the National Security Council issue, revoke, suspend, or adjudicate security clearances, except where acting through a lawful process expressly authorized by statute.

(c) Authority to initiate a determination.—A determination may be initiated only by the Attorney General; the Director of National Intelligence; the Secretary of Homeland Security; the Secretary of Defense where the covered position concerns military, defense, or Department of Defense access; or a Senate-confirmed deputy or principal national security officer expressly designated in writing by one of those officials. A designee may initiate a determination only under a written delegation retained as an official record and transmitted to the appropriate Inspector General.

(d) Emergency temporary suspension.—Any emergency temporary suspension shall be supported by a written statement identifying the imminent risk, the scope of the suspension, and the reason ordinary procedures could not adequately prevent the risk.

(e) Inspector General notice.—Within 24 hours after imposing an emergency temporary suspension, the initiating official shall transmit notice to the appropriate Inspector General. Such notice may be classified where necessary.

(f) Repeated suspensions.—An emergency temporary suspension may not be repeatedly reissued against the same subject on substantially the same factual basis for the purpose of avoiding notice, hearing, review, or final decision requirements under this Title.

(g) Public disclosure oversight.—Any public disclosure made under this subsection shall be transmitted to the appropriate congressional committees and the appropriate Inspector General not later than 48 hours after disclosure, together with the written determination supporting such disclosure.
(h) Judicial review deadline.—An action for judicial review of final agency action under the National Security Act of 2026 shall be filed not later than 14 days after final agency action.

(i) Regulatory limitation.—Regulations implementing national security eligibility procedures may not reduce statutory procedural rights and may not authorize automatic clearance, automatic compartmented access, public threat designation without process, or any eligibility restriction inconsistent with law.

sections.heading: Compartmented and special-access information
paragraphs: (a) No person shall receive, retain, or exercise Sensitive Compartmented Information access, Special Access Program access, Department Sensitive Information access, or any other compartmented or controlled access solely by virtue of holding a public office, military command, judicial assignment, congressional position, employment title, statutory office, or contract role.
(b) Compartmented access shall require—
(i) a lawful clearance eligibility determination;
(ii) a need-to-know determination;
(iii) approval by the owner, administrator, or lawful authority responsible for the compartment or program; and
(iv) compliance with all applicable handling, storage, disclosure, and access restrictions.

(c) Nothing in this section shall prohibit senior officials from receiving compartmented access when necessary for the performance of official duties, provided that such access is authorized by the appropriate security authority and remains subject to need-to-know, compartment controls, review, suspension, and revocation.

(d) A security clearance, including a Top Secret clearance, shall not by itself authorize access to Sensitive Compartmented Information, Special Access Program information, Department Sensitive Information, or any other compartmented information without specific access approval.

sections.heading: Expedited review for officials requiring urgent access
paragraphs: (a) The Director of National Intelligence may establish expedited clearance, access, and eligibility review procedures for officials whose duties require urgent or continuous access to classified or protected national security information.

(b) An expedited process established under subsection (a) shall not constitute automatic clearance, automatic access, waiver of need-to-know requirements, waiver of compartment approval, or exemption from later review.
(c) Temporary or interim access may be granted under expedited procedures only where—
(i) access is required for official duties;
(ii) the scope of access is limited to the minimum information necessary;
(iii) the access is documented;
(iv) the access is time-limited; and
(v) the access remains subject to suspension, revocation, or limitation.

(d) The Director of National Intelligence shall maintain records of all expedited, temporary, or interim access granted under this section, including the official receiving access, the authorizing official, the scope of access, the duration of access, and the justification for expedited handling.

sections.heading: Inspector General and congressional oversight of national security eligibility actions
paragraphs: (a) The appropriate Inspector General shall have access to notices, evidence summaries, emergency suspension memoranda, adjudicative decisions, renewal determinations, public disclosure determinations, and other records necessary to review compliance with national security eligibility and clearance procedures.
(b) An Inspector General with jurisdiction may review whether a national security eligibility action, clearance action, access restriction, emergency suspension, or public disclosure was—
(i) supported by evidence;
(ii) properly tailored;
(iii) procedurally compliant;
(iv) Non-retaliatory;
(v) consistent with statutory rights; and
(vi) free from political, personal, or improper influence.

(c) Not less than once every 30 days, the Attorney General, Director of National Intelligence, Secretary of Homeland Security, and Secretary of Defense shall provide the appropriate congressional committees with a classified or unclassified report stating—
(i) the number of national security eligibility determinations initiated;
(ii) the number of emergency temporary suspensions imposed;
(iii) the number of final determinations issued;
(iv) the number of determinations modified, removed, or allowed to expire;
(v) the number of expedited access approvals granted;
(vi) the number of judicial review actions filed;
(vii) the number of public disclosures made under operational necessity authority; and
(viii) any substantiated abuse, procedural failure, retaliation finding, or corrective action.
(d) Reports required under this section may be classified, but classification shall not be used to withhold the existence of the report from the appropriate congressional committees.

(e) Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit lawful access by Inspectors General, courts, or congressional committees acting within their jurisdiction, subject to lawful security handling procedures.

sections.heading: Anti-retaliation protection in national security eligibility actions
paragraphs: (a) No national security eligibility determination, emergency suspension, clearance action, access restriction, public disclosure, referral, or adverse administrative action may be initiated, maintained, renewed, or disclosed for the purpose of retaliating against—
(i) protected whistleblowing;
(ii) lawful reporting to an Inspector General;
(iii) lawful congressional testimony or communication;
(iv) protected speech;
(v) lawful political association;
(vi) refusal to violate law; or
(vii) exercise of constitutional or statutory rights.

(b) Where a subject presents credible evidence that an action covered by subsection (a) was retaliatory, the adjudicator, reviewing official, or court shall specifically address the retaliation claim in writing.

(c) If retaliation is found, the action shall be set aside, the record shall be corrected, improper disclosures shall be withdrawn or corrected to the maximum extent practicable, and the subject shall receive any further relief authorized by law.
(d) Nothing in this section shall prevent lawful action based on genuine national security risk, provided that such action is supported by evidence and taken in compliance with applicable procedures.

sections.heading: Classification and oversight safeguards
paragraphs: (a) The classified, protected, compartmented, or sensitive nature of information shall not, by itself, be sufficient grounds to deny lawful access to Inspectors General, courts, or congressional committees acting within their jurisdiction, subject to lawful handling and security procedures.
(b) Information may not be classified, reclassified, marked, withheld, or compartmented for the purpose of—
(i) concealing misconduct;
(ii) preventing embarrassment;
(iii) avoiding oversight;
(iv) defeating judicial review;
(v) restricting lawful whistleblower disclosures;
(vi) suppressing protected speech; or
(vii) preventing lawful disclosure of non-protected information.

(c) Where a record contains both protected and non-protected information, agencies shall segregate the protected information and release, summarize, substitute, or otherwise provide the non-protected portions to the maximum extent feasible.
(d) Protected national security information shall be marked, stored, transmitted, accessed, and destroyed according to applicable classification and control marking rules.
